summary: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian, speaking with Kara Swisher at the University of Virginia, criticized the current social media landscape and creator economy for rewarding likes, speed and misinformation. He still calls himself a "techno-optimist" and believes the pendulum will swing back, with a revival of in-person experiences and better-aware founders. He also discussed his 2020 Reddit board resignation, Reddit's growth, Community Notes on X, TikTok, and the flawed "town square" analogy.
one_line: Alexis Ohanian, despite criticizing social media's harms, tells Kara Swisher he remains a techno-optimist who expects a swing back toward healthier, more human platforms.
key_facts: Alexis Ohanian, Reddit co-founder and founder of venture fund Seven Seven Six (776), spoke at an event at the University of Virginia in an interview with Kara Swisher.
Ohanian said people have been "so trained and conditioned now to just get the likes and retweets, get the upvotes."
He called himself a "techno-optimist" ("Guilty as charged"), echoing a16z General Partner Marc Andreessen's recent claim that technology could solve all our problems.
Ohanian thinks the pendulum will swing back "even swifter than we realize," and the war in the Middle East may be a tipping point.
Ohanian resigned from Reddit's board in 2020 over differences on moderation and cracking down on communities about violence and hate, asking that his seat go to a Black board member.
Reddit appointed Y Combinator partner Michael Seibel as its first Black board member after Ohanian's resignation.
Reddit later banned toxic communities including r/donaldtrup after violence at the U.S. Capitol, and Ohanian says the site has "gotten demonstrably better," including as a business.
Ohanian said Reddit grew out of a forum site he ran in college, and that imagining it would affect democracy would have been "ludicrous"; he called it a "blind spot."
He called TikTok "an arm for the Chinese government" that is good at "feeding us what we want, when we want it."
Ohanian called X's Community Notes "the best measure I've seen yet" for moderation and said he wishes Reddit had thought of it first.
He argued the "public square" analogy for X falls flat because the CEO would be like a king or "infinite dictator" with no democratic election.
Ohanian predicts a "rebirth of live gatherings and in-person experiences" and says founders 776 invests in are smarter and more aware of the issues than he was at their age.
